Subject: Follow-up: Data retention / deletion SLAs & SOC 2 status

Hi Liam / Amaya security team —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap + a few asks so we can move the security review forward: 

- SOC 2: you mentioned Amaya requests SOC 2 Type II report. Can you confirm the specific scope (CC1 only, or CC1 + CC2?) and whether a self-attestation is acceptable while you await the latest report?
- GDPR / HIPAA: confirm whether you'll need a BAA and any specific data processing addenda beyond our standard terms.
- Vendor questionnaire: I’ve attached our vendor security questionnaire (partial) for you to kick off. If you can point us to your preferred format we can convert/complete.
- Data retention & deletion: you asked about primary data deletion SLA and backups — see the initial answers below. If you need changes we can surface options (shorter/longer retention or account-level config + contract language).

Initial answers (high-level):
- Primary customer data: deletion requested will be actioned within 30 days by default (primary datastore).
- Backups / snapshots: backups are retained for up to 90 days by default; in many cases backups are immutable and deletion requires retention-window expiry — we can discuss contractual limits (e.g., 30 / 90 / 180 days).
- Audit logs & request logs: default 90 days; configurable up to 1 year for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Next steps we propose:
1) Amaya confirms SOC 2 scope + required timeline.
2) We exchange vendor questionnaire (I attached our sheet; I can also fill Amaya's if you send it).
3) Loop in Rishi (sales engineering) and Neha (security) for any deeper technical clarifications or to schedule a short follow-up call.

Attaching: Redwood_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_partial.xlsx (stub)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with Rishi and Neha on any technical notes.

Best,

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the summary and the questionnaire. Quick answers from our side:

- SOC 2: We require SOC 2 Type II covering CC1 + CC2 where applicable. We have the report for our platform vendor stack, but we typically need vendor-specific evidence. If you can provide a SOC 2 summary or bridge letter (Type II or Type I + evidence), that helps while your full Type II is available.
- BAA / HIPAA: Yes — we will need a BAA for PHI flows. Please send your standard BAA template or link to the DPA/processing addendum.
- Backups: procurement asked for explicit language about backups being deleted within X days of request. We need clarity on whether backup deletion can be guaranteed within 90 days or if there are cases where recovery windows exceed that.

Also, procurement prefers we use our vendor questionnaire (attached to their ticket). Can your team fill it in? If not, we can start with yours and then map answers.

Can you confirm when Rishi / Neha might be available for a 30-minute follow-up next week? We also need a quick note on log retention windows and whether logs used for debugging are retained separately from customer data backups.

Thanks — Liam
Liam O'Connor
Security Manager | Amaya Health

Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data retention / deletion SLAs & SOC 2 status

Hi Liam / team —

Looping Rishi and Neha in as discussed. Answers below with a bit more precision. We attached a short SOC 2 summary (not the full Type II PDF) and a partially completed vendor questionnaire to speed things up.

SOC 2 / attestations
- Redwood status: We completed SOC 2 Type I (security) in 2025 and have a SOC 2 Type II audit underway; we expect Type II attestation for the core control set in Q4 2026. In the meantime we can provide a SOC 2 bridge letter and our security control matrix. The attached "Redwood_SOC2_summary_2026Q2.pdf" includes the control coverage and recent pen-test highlights.

HIPAA / BAA
- We do execute BAAs. I’ve linked our standard BAA in the related_links list (DocuSign). If Amaya has specific contractual language we can review; otherwise we can send our template for signature.

Data retention / deletion (primary + backups) — default platform behavior and options:
- Primary data (customer-managed datasets, model request payloads, user content): when a deletion request is accepted we remove data from the primary datastore within 30 calendar days by default. We can support accelerated deletion SLA (15 days) for enterprise contracts with an addendum.
- Backups / snapshots: by default backups are retained for 90 days; backup immutability means restoration can occur until retention expiry. We can contractually limit backup retention to 30 / 90 / 180 days depending on account tier. Note that immutable backup artifacts may require the retention window to lapse; we can include explicit language in the contract to limit retention to X days post-termination/deletion request.
- Audit & request logs: default 90 days. For Dedicated and Private deployments we can configure up to 365 days. Logs used solely for debugging are logically separated from customer data and can be retained on different windows; we’ll work with you to define which log classes (request logs, system logs, debug traces) are subject to which retention window.

Other notes:
- Deletion proofs: we can provide deletion certificates and logs showing when deletion tasks were executed.
- Encryption & key management: data-at-rest is encrypted; for dedicated/private deployments we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM).

Attachments included (stubs):
- Redwood_SOC2_summary_2026Q2.pdf
- Redwood_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_partial.xlsx

Next steps (proposed):
1) Rishi / Neha to review Amaya vendor questionnaire (if you attach it, we’ll map answers into your sheet).
2) Schedule 30-min follow-up next week to confirm backup retention language and BAA path. Rishi: are you available Tues 8/18 or Wed 8/19 morning PDT?
3) If Amaya confirms a 30-day backup deletion requirement, we’ll prepare proposed contract language and a short technical note on operational implications (immutability / restore windows).

Rishi / Neha — any technical clarifications to add?

Thanks,
Marissa

- Do deletion certificates include backup artifacts or only primary datastore removal logs?

Look forward to the call — Liam
